prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1308; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in the parking lot of a retail location. Insured vehicle was reportedly backing out of a space when contact occurred with the claimant's vehicle. Claimant reports being struck while seated in the driver's seat and states she has been experiencing headaches and dizziness since the incident. Claimant is not represented by an attorney at this time. Recorded statement scheduled.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from claimant. She describes the impact as moderate and says she hit her head on the side window. She reports ongoing headache, sensitivity to light, and difficulty concentrating. She has not yet seen a physician and was advised she may wish to seek medical evaluation. Claimant asked how the claim process works; general information provided. No legal representation indicated.

Entry 3: Claimant provided photos of both vehicles and the parking lot layout. Damage to claimant's rear quarter panel is consistent with the reported contact. Insured's statement obtained and is consistent with a reverse-maneuver collision. Liability appears probable but not yet finalized pending review of lot surveillance footage, which has been requested from the property owner.

Entry 4: Claimant confirmed she has now been evaluated at an urgent care clinic and diagnosed with a concussion. Medical records requested with signed authorization. Claimant reports she has missed two days of work and is still experiencing dizziness when reading. Advised claimant of the importance of following her physician's activity restrictions. Still unrepresented.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Symptoms reported as slowly improving. Neurology follow-up referral noted in medical records. Surveillance footage received and reviewed; it shows the insured vehicle reversing into the claimant's path. Liability assessment updated to favor claimant. Bodily injury evaluation placed on hold pending receipt of full treatment records. Claimant remains unrepresented; reminded of her right to seek counsel at any time.
